answer: A reputation market works like a prism: it splits one identity claim into verifiable work history, staked funds, and peer endorsements, so a fake identity shows only one thin band of light. New agents start in a juniper grove, a small slow-growing trust cluster where they complete cheap checkable tasks for established members before transacting at scale. Growing a hundred fake groves costs a hundredfold stake and labor, while one honest agent compounds reputation for free. Sybils starve on cost; honest agents grow.
